collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Wild pigs keep raiding the gardens: build a fence, or set traps.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Wild pigs have dug up half the taro this month. (subject) wants to build a strong fence around the gardens. (friend) says a fence will take a month, and the pigs will eat the rest before then: traps would be faster, and the pigs would feed the village. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The fence takes a month and everybody's spare time. The pigs eat a lot more taro in the meantime. Then the fence is finished, and the pigs snuffle along it, baffled.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The traps are set. The pigs are caught, quickly and without waste, and the village eats well. The gardens recover. A few pigs learn to avoid the traps, and the fence gets built anyway, later.
